Classification of the solutions of a mixed nonlinear Schrödinger system

Abstract

In this paper, we study a couple of NLS equations characterized by mixed cubic and superlinear power laws. Classification of the solutions as well as existence and uniqueness of the steady state solutions have been investigated.

Keywords: 
Variational, Energy functional, Existence, Uniqueness, NLS system, Classification.
PACS
35Q41; 35J50

1 Introduction

The paper is devoted to the study of some nonlinear systems of PDEs of the form

{L1(u)+f1(u,v)=0,ℒ2(v)+f2(u,v)=0\cases{}{L}_{1}(u)+f_{1}(u,v)=0,\\ \mathcal{L}_{2}(v)+f_{2}(u,v)=0 (1)

where u=u⁡(x,t)u=u(x,t), v=v⁡(x,t)v=v(x,t) on a domain Ω×(t0,+∞)\Omega\times(t_{0},+\infty), Ω⊂ℝN\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{N}, t0∈ℝt_{0}\in\mathbb{R} with suitable initial and boundary conditions. The operators ℒ1\mathcal{L}_{1} and ℒ2\mathcal{L}_{2} are linear Schrödinger-type operators of the form

ℒi(u(x,t))=iut+σiux​x,i=1,2\mathcal{L}_{i}(u(x,t))=iu_{t}+\sigma_{i}u_{xx},\;i=1,2

leading to a nonlinear Schrödinger system. ux​xu_{xx} is the second order partial derivative relatively to xx, which plays the role of the Laplacian, utu_{t} is the first order partial derivative in time, σi\sigma_{i}, i=1,2i=1,2 are constant real positive parameters. f1f_{1} and f2f_{2} are nonlinear continuous functions of two variables.

Remark that whenever the ℒi\mathcal{L}_{i}’s are the classical Schrödinger operators

ℒ1​(u)=ℒ2​(u)=i​ut+ux​x\mathcal{L}_{1}(u)=\mathcal{L}_{2}(u)=iu_{t}+u_{xx}

and u=v=φu=v=\varphi, f1=f2=ff_{1}=f_{2}=f, we come back to the original Schrödinger equation

i​φt+Δ​φ=f⁡(φ).i\varphi_{t}+\Delta\varphi=f(\varphi). (2)

On the other hand, this last equation itself may lead to a system of PDEs of real valued functions satisfying a Heat system. Indeed, let φ=u+i​v=(1+i)​u\varphi=u+iv=(1+i)u, we get a system of coupled Heat ones

{ut−Δ​u+f1​(u,v)=0.vt+Δ​v+f2​(u,v)=0,\cases{u}_{t}-\Delta u+f_{1}(u,v)=0.\\ v_{t}+\Delta v+f_{2}(u,v)=0, (3)

where f1f_{1} and f2f_{2} are issued from the real and imagiary parts of f⁡(φ)f(\varphi).

Return again to the system (1) in the simple case σi=1\sigma_{i}=1 and denote φ=u+i​v\varphi=u+iv and f⁡(φ)=f1​(u,v)+i​f2​(u,v)f(\varphi)=f_{1}(u,v)+if_{2}(u,v), we come back to the classical NLS equation where uu and vv may be seen as real and imaginary parts of the solution φ\varphi of an equation of the form (2).

As it is related to many physical/natural phenomena such as plasma, optics, condensed matter physics, etc, nonlinear Schrödinger system has attracted the interest of researchers in different fields such as pure and applied mathematics, pure and applied physics, quantum mechanics, mathematical physics, and it continues to attract resaerchers nowadays with the discovery of nano-physics, fractal domains, planets understanding, … etc. For instence, in hydrodynamics, the NLS system may be a good model to describe the propagation of packets of waves according to some directions where a phenomenon of overlopping group velocity projection may occur [20]. In optics also, the propagation of short pulses has been investigated via a system of NLS equations [28].

In single NLS equation, studies have been well developed from both theoretical and numerical aspects. The most recent mixed model is developed in [8], [9], [10], [11], [12], [13], [14], [15], [24], [25], [27], [29], [41], [42], … with a general model

f⁡(u)=|u|p−1​u+λ​|u|q−1​u.f(u)=|u|^{p-1}u+\lambda|u|^{q-1}u.

which coincides with f⁡(u,u)f(u,u) in the model (4). An extending interesting model will be a mixed model of nonlinearities

f⁡(u,v)=(|u|p−1+λ​|v|q−1)​u,p,q,λ∈ℝ.f(u,v)=(|u|^{p-1}+\lambda|v|^{q-1})u,\;\;p,q,\lambda\in\mathbb{R}. (4)

In the literature, few works are done on such a model and are focusing on the mixed cubic-cubic (p=q=3p=q=3) one

f⁡(u,v)=(|u|2+λ​|v|2)​u.f(u,v)=(|u|^{2}+\lambda|v|^{2})u.

For example, in [43], (2+1)-dimensional coupled NLS equations have been studied based on symbolic computation and Hirota method via the cubic-cubic nonlinear system

{i​ut+ux​x+σ⁡(|u|2+α​|v|2)​u=0,i​vt+vx​x+σ⁡(|v|2+α​|u|2)​v=0,\left\{\begin{array}[]{lll}iu_{t}+u_{xx}+\sigma(|u|^{2}+\alpha|v|^{2})u=0,\\ iv_{t}+v_{xx}+\sigma(|v|^{2}+\alpha|u|^{2})v=0,\end{array}\right. (5)

where α\alpha and σ\sigma are real parameters. The same system has been also studied by many authors such as [1], [19], [22], [23], [30], [39]. In [44], the following more general system has been investigated for the asymptotic time behavior of the solutions,

{i​∂tu+α​∂x2u+A⁡(|u|2+|v|2)​u=0,i​∂tv+α​∂x2v+A⁡(|u|2+|v|2)​v=0\left\{\begin{array}[]{lll}i\partial_{t}u+\alpha\partial_{x}^{2}u+A(|u|^{2}+|v|^{2})u=0,\\ i\partial_{t}v+\alpha\partial_{x}^{2}v+A(|u|^{2}+|v|^{2})v=0\\ \end{array}\right. (6)

See also [21]. In [18] the following pp-Laplacian stationary system has been discussed for necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of the solutions

{−Δp​u=μ1​Γ1​(x,u,v)​in​ℝN−Δp​v=μ2​Γ2​(x,u,v)​in​ℝN,\left\{\begin{array}[]{c}-\Delta_{p}u=\mu_{1}\Gamma_{1}(x,u,v)~~\hbox{in}~~\mathbb{R}^{N}\\ -\Delta_{p}v=\mu_{2}\Gamma_{2}(x,u,v)~~\hbox{in}~~\mathbb{R}^{N},\end{array}\right. (7)

where Δpu=div(|∇u|p−2∇u)\Delta_{p}u=div(|\nabla u|^{p-2}\nabla u) is the pp-Laplacian (1<p<N)(1<p<N). In [6], solutions of the type

u⁡(x,t)=u⁡(x)​ei​w​t,u(x,t)=u(x)e^{iwt}, (8)

where uu is a real function known as standing wave or steady state and w∈ℝw\in\mathbb{R} has been investigated leading to the time-independent problem

−Δ​u+(m02−ω2)​u−|u|p−2​u=0-\Delta u+(m_{0}^{2}-\omega^{2})u-|u|^{p-2}u=0 (9)

See also [40]. Already with the familiar cubic-cubic case, numerical solutions have been developed in [45] for the one-dimensional system

{i​∂u∂t+12​∂2u∂x2+(|u|2+β​|v|2)​u=0,i​∂v∂t+12​∂2v∂x2+(β​|u|2+|v|2)​v=0,u⁡(x,0)=u0​(x)v⁡(x,0)=v0​(x).\left\{\begin{array}[]{l}i\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}+\frac{1}{2}\frac{\partial^{2}u}{\partial x^{2}}+(|u|^{2}+\beta|v|^{2})u=0,\\ i\frac{\partial v}{\partial t}+\frac{1}{2}\frac{\partial^{2}v}{\partial x^{2}}+(\beta|u|^{2}+|v|^{2})v=0,\\ u(x,0)=u_{0}(x)~~~~~~v(x,0)=v_{0}(x).\end{array}\right. (10)

on ℝ\mathbb{R}, where uu and vv stands for the wave amplitude considered in two polarizations. The parameter β\beta is related to phase modulation. u0u_{0} and v0v_{0} are fixed functions assumed to be sufficiently regular.

Coupled NLS system has been analyzed for symmetries and exact solutions in [34]. The problem studied is related to atmospheric gravity waves governed by the following general coupled NLS system.

{i​ut+α1​ux​x+(σ1​|u|2+Γ1​|v|2)​u=0,i​vt+i​C​vx+α2​vx​x+(Γ2​|u|2+σ2​|v|2)​v=0.\left\{\begin{array}[]{l}iu_{t}+\alpha_{1}u_{xx}+(\sigma_{1}|u|^{2}+\Gamma_{1}|v|^{2})u=0,\\ iv_{t}+iCv_{x}+\alpha_{2}v_{xx}+(\Gamma_{2}|u|^{2}+\sigma_{2}|v|^{2})v=0.\end{array}\right. (11)

It is noticed that such a problem may be transformed to the wall known Boussinesq equation.

In [2], novel effective approach for systems of coupled NLS equations has been developed for the model problem

{i​ut+i​ux+ux​x+u+v+σ1​f​(u,v)​u=0,i​vt−i​vx+vx​x+u−v+σ2​g​(u,v)​v=0,\left\{\begin{array}[]{lll}iu_{t}+iu_{x}+u_{xx}+u+v+\sigma_{1}f(u,v)u=0,\\ iv_{t}-iv_{x}+v_{xx}+u-v+\sigma_{2}g(u,v)v=0,\end{array}\right. (12)

where ff and gg are smooth nonlinear real functions depending on (|u|2,|v|2)(|u|^{2},|v|^{2}) and σ1\sigma_{1}, σ2\sigma_{2} are parameters. In [33], the folowing nonlinear cubic-quintic and coupling quintic system of NLS equations has been examined,

{ut+m1​ux​x=(α+i​β)​u+f1​|u|2​u+f2​|u|4​u+f3​|v|2​u+f4​|u|2​|v|2​u,vt+m2​vx​x=(γ+i​δ)​v+g1​|v|2​v+g2​|v|4​v+g3​|u|2​v+g4​|u|2​|v|2​v,\left\{\begin{array}[]{lll}u_{t}+m_{1}u_{xx}=(\alpha+i\beta)u+f_{1}|u|^{2}u+f_{2}|u|^{4}u+f_{3}|v|^{2}u+f_{4}|u|^{2}|v|^{2}u,\\ v_{t}+m_{2}v_{xx}=(\gamma+i\delta)v+g_{1}|v|^{2}v+g_{2}|v|^{4}v+g_{3}|u|^{2}v+g_{4}|u|^{2}|v|^{2}v,\\ \end{array}\right. (13)

where uu and vv describe the complex envelopes of an electric field in a co-moving frame. α\alpha and γ\gamma are potentials. β\beta and δ\delta are amplifications. The functions fjf_{j} and gjg_{j}, j=1,1,3,4j=1,1,3,4 describe the cubic, quintic and coupling quintic nonlinearities coefficients respectively. m1m_{1} and m2m_{2} stands for the dispersion parameters

In [26], existence of ground state solutions has been studied for the NLS system

{−i​∂∂t​ψ1=Δ​ψ1−v1​(x)​ψ1+μ1​|ψ1|2​ψ1+β​|ψ2|2​ψ1+γ​ψ2,−i​∂∂t​ψ2=Δ​ψ2−v2​(x)​ψ2+μ2​|ψ1|2​ψ2+β​|ψ1|2​ψ2+γ​ψ1,ψj=ψj​(x,t)∈ℂ,\left\{\begin{array}[]{lll}-i\frac{\partial}{\partial t}\psi_{1}=\Delta\psi_{1}-v_{1}(x)\psi_{1}+\mu_{1}|\psi_{1}|^{2}\psi_{1}+\beta|\psi_{2}|^{2}\psi_{1}+\gamma\psi_{2},\\ -i\frac{\partial}{\partial t}\psi_{2}=\Delta\psi_{2}-v_{2}(x)\psi_{2}+\mu_{2}|\psi_{1}|^{2}\psi_{2}+\beta|\psi_{1}|^{2}\psi_{2}+\gamma\psi_{1},\\ \psi_{j}=\psi_{j}(x,t)\in\mathbb{C},\end{array}\right. (14)

x∈ℝx\in\mathbb{R}, t>0t>0, j=1,2j=1,2.

In [37] a multi-nonlinearities coupled focusing NLS system has been studied for existence of ground state solutions and global existence and finite-time blow-up solutions. The authors considered precisely the coupled system

{iu˙j+Δuj=−∑mk=1aj​k|uk|p−2uj,uj(0,.)=ψj\left\{\begin{array}[]{l}i\dot{u}_{j}+\Delta u_{j}=-\displaystyle\sum^{m}_{k=1}a_{jk}|u_{k}|^{p-2}u_{j},\\ u_{j}(0,.)=\psi_{j}\end{array}\right. (15)

where uj:ℝN×ℝ→ℂu_{j}:\mathbb{R}^{N}\times\mathbb{R}\rightarrow\mathbb{C}, j=1,2,…,mj=1,2,\dots,m and the aj​ka_{jk}’s are positive real numbers with aj​k=ak​ja_{jk}=a_{kj}.

In the present work, we focus on the nonlinear mixed super-linear cubic defocusing model

f1​(u,v)=g⁡(u,v)​u=(|u|p−1+λ​|v|2)​u=f2​(v,u),f_{1}(u,v)=g(u,v)u=(|u|^{p-1}+\lambda|v|^{2})u=f_{2}(v,u), (16)

with λ>0\lambda>0 and 1<p≠31<p\not=3. We consider the evolutive nonlinear Schrödinger system on ℝ×(0,+∞)\mathbb{R}\times(0,+\infty),

{i​ut+σ1​ux​x+g⁡(u,v)​u=0,i​vt+σ2​vx​x+g⁡(v,u)​v=0.\left\{\begin{array}[]{lll}iu_{t}+\sigma_{1}u_{xx}+g(u,v)u=0,\\ iv_{t}+\sigma_{2}v_{xx}+g(v,u)v=0.\end{array}\right. (17)

Focuses will be on the study of the behavior of the steady state solutions according to their initial values. We propose precisely to develop a classification of the steady state solutions of problem (17). Recall that a steady state solution of problem (17) is any solution of the form

W⁡(x,t)=(ei​ω​t​u​(x),ei​ω​t​v​(x)),W(x,t)=(e^{i\omega t}u(x),e^{i\omega t}v(x)),

ω>0\omega>0. Substituting WW in problem (17), we immediately obtain a solution (u,v)(u,v) of the system

{σ1​ux​x−ω​u+g⁡(u,v)​u=0,σ2​vx​x−ω​v+g⁡(v,u)​v=0.\cases{\sigma}_{1}u_{xx}-\omega u+g(u,v)u=0,\\ \sigma_{2}v_{xx}-\omega v+g(v,u)v=0. (18)

We will see that classifying the solutions of problem (18) depends strongly on the positoive/negative/null zones of the nonlinear function

gω​(x,y)=|x|p−1+λ​y2−ω,(x,y)∈ℝ2g_{\omega}(x,y)=|x|^{p-1}+\lambda y^{2}-\omega,\;\;(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^{2}

which in turns varies accordingly to the parameters pp, λ\lambda and ω\omega. Denote also for s∈ℝs\in\mathbb{R}, s≠1s\not=1 and η>0\eta>0, ωs,η=(ωη)1s−1\omega_{s,\eta}=\left(\displaystyle\frac{\omega}{\eta}\right)^{\frac{1}{s-1}}. Denote also

Γp,λω={(u,v)∈ℝ2;|u|p−1+λv2−ω=0}\Gamma^{\omega}_{p,\lambda}=\left\{(u,v)\in\mathbb{R}^{2}\,;\;|u|^{p-1}+\lambda v^{2}-\omega=0\right\}

and

Γp,λω,∗={(u,v)∈ℝ2;|v|p−1+λu2−ω=0}.\Gamma^{\omega,*}_{p,\lambda}=\left\{(u,v)\in\mathbb{R}^{2}\,;\;|v|^{p-1}+\lambda u^{2}-\omega=0\right\}.

It is noticeable that such curves are more and more smooth whenever the parameter pp increases. To illustrate this fact, we provided in Appendix 4.2 a brief overvew for some cases of Γp,λω\Gamma^{\omega}_{p,\lambda} and Γp,λω,∗\Gamma^{\omega,*}_{p,\lambda}.

The paper is organized as follows. The next section is concerned with the development of our main results. Concluding and future directions are next raised in section 3. An appendix is also developed to illustrate the effects of the parameters of the problem on the classification of the solutions.

2 Main results

As it is said in the introduction, the behavior of the solutions depends strongly on the parameters of the problem, especially those affacting the sign of the function gωg_{\omega}. It holds in fact that some of these parameters may be reduced to

σ1=σ2=λ=1,\sigma_{1}=\sigma_{2}=\lambda=1,

which simplifies the computations needed later. Indeed, denote

u⁡(r)=u~​(rσ1)andv⁡(r)=v~​(rσ2),u(r)=\widetilde{u}(\displaystyle\frac{r}{\sqrt{\sigma}_{1}})\quad\hbox{and}\quad v(r)=\widetilde{v}(\displaystyle\frac{r}{\sqrt{\sigma}_{2}}),

the functions u~\widetilde{u} and v~\widetilde{v} satisfy immediately the system

ux​x−ω​u+g⁡(u,v)​u=0,vx​x−ω​v+g⁡(v,u)​v=0.{u}_{xx}-\omega{u}+g({u},{v}){u}=0,\qquad{v}_{xx}-\omega{v}+g({v},{u}){v}=0.

Moreover, consider the scaling modifications

u⁡(r)=K1​u¯​(α​r)andv⁡(r)=K2​v¯​(β​r),u(r)=K_{1}\overline{u}(\alpha r)\quad\hbox{and}\quad v(r)=K_{2}\overline{v}(\beta r),

where K1K_{1}, K2K_{2}, α\alpha and β\beta are constants to be fixed. The functions u¯\overline{u} and v¯\overline{v} satisfy the system

{ux​x+(|u|p−1+|v|2−ω)​u=0,vx​x+(|v|p−1+|u|2−ω)​v=0,\cases{u}_{xx}+(|u|^{p-1}+|v|^{2}-\omega)u=0,\\ v_{xx}+(|v|^{p-1}+|u|^{2}-\omega)v=0,\\ (19)

whenever the constants K1K_{1}, K2K_{2}, α\alpha and β\beta satisfy

K1p−1=σ1​α2,K2p−1=σ2​β2,λ​K12=σ2​β2,λ​K22=σ1​α2,K_{1}^{p-1}=\sigma_{1}\alpha^{2},\;\;K_{2}^{p-1}=\sigma_{2}\beta^{2},\;\;\lambda K_{1}^{2}=\sigma_{2}\beta^{2},\;\;\lambda K_{2}^{2}=\sigma_{1}\alpha^{2}, (20)

which in turns yields that

α=exp⁡((p−1)​Bλ​(σ1,σ2)−2​Aλ​(σ1,σ2)(p−3)​(p+1)),\alpha=\exp\bigl(\displaystyle\frac{(p-1)B_{\lambda}(\sigma_{1},\sigma_{2})-2A_{\lambda}(\sigma_{1},\sigma_{2})}{(p-3)(p+1)}\bigr),
β=exp⁡(2​Bλ​(σ1,σ2)−(p−1)​Aλ​(σ1,σ2)(p−3)​(p+1)),\beta=\exp\bigl(\displaystyle\frac{2B_{\lambda}(\sigma_{1},\sigma_{2})-(p-1)A_{\lambda}(\sigma_{1},\sigma_{2})}{(p-3)(p+1)}\bigr),
K1=σ2​β2λ​and​K2=σ1​α2λ,K_{1}=\sqrt{\displaystyle\frac{\sigma_{2}\beta^{2}}{\lambda}}\;\;\hbox{and}\;\;K_{2}=\sqrt{\displaystyle\frac{\sigma_{1}\alpha^{2}}{\lambda}},

where

Aλ​(σ1,σ2)=11−p​log⁡σ1+12​log⁡σ2−12​log⁡λA_{\lambda}(\sigma_{1},\sigma_{2})=\displaystyle\frac{1}{1-p}\log\sigma_{1}+\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\log\sigma_{2}-\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\log\lambda

and

Bλ​(σ1,σ2)=−12​log⁡σ1+1p−1​log⁡σ2−12​log⁡λ.B_{\lambda}(\sigma_{1},\sigma_{2})=-\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\log\sigma_{1}+\displaystyle\frac{1}{p-1}\log\sigma_{2}-\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\log\lambda.

Given these facts, we will consider in the rest of the paper the problem (19) with the initial conditions

u⁡(0)=a,v⁡(0)=b,u′​(0)=v′​(0)=0,u(0)=a\,,\;v(0)=b\,,\;\;u^{\prime}(0)=v^{\prime}(0)=0, (21)

where a,b∈ℝa,b\in\mathbb{R}. The associated curves will be denoted simply

Γp,ω={(u,v)∈ℝ2;|u|p−1+|v|2−ω=0}\Gamma_{p,\omega}=\left\{(u,v)\in\mathbb{R}^{2}\,;\;|u|^{p-1}+|v|^{2}-\omega=0\right\}

and

Γp,ω∗={(u,v)∈ℝ2;|v|p−1+|u|2−ω=0}\Gamma^{*}_{p,\omega}=\left\{(u,v)\in\mathbb{R}^{2}\,;\;|v|^{p-1}+|u|^{2}-\omega=0\right\}

and

Λp={(u,v)∈ℝ2;|u|p−1+|v|2=|v|p−1+|u|2}.\Lambda_{p}=\left\{(u,v)\in\mathbb{R}^{2}\,;\;|u|^{p-1}+|v|^{2}=|v|^{p-1}+|u|^{2}\right\}.

Denote also ωs=ω1s−1\omega_{s}=\omega^{\frac{1}{s-1}}, for s∈ℝs\in\mathbb{R}, s≠1s\not=1. Figure 1 illustrates the partition of the plane ℝ2\mathbb{R}^{2} according to the curves Γp,ω\Gamma_{p,\omega} and Γp,ω∗\Gamma^{*}_{p,\omega}. Figure 2 illustrates the partition of the plane ℝ2\mathbb{R}^{2} according to the curve Λp\Lambda_{p}. Finally, Figure 3 illustrates the partition of the plane ℝ2\mathbb{R}^{2} according to all the curves Λp,ω\Lambda_{p,\omega}, Γp,ω∗\Gamma^{*}_{p,\omega} and Λp\Lambda_{p}.

We now start developing our main results. For this aim, we assume in the rest of the paper that

ω≥1​and​  1<p<3.\omega\geq 1\;\;\hbox{and}\;\;1<p<3. (22)

It is straightforward that ωp>ω3\omega_{p}>\omega_{3}. Moreover, the closed curves Γp,ω\Gamma_{p,\omega} and Γp,ω∗\Gamma^{*}_{p,\omega} intersect at four points BB, DD, FF and HH as it is shown in Figure 1. Notice also that the curves Γp,ω\Gamma_{p,\omega} and Γp,ω∗\Gamma^{*}_{p,\omega} split the plane (u,v)(u,v) into twelve regions, Ωi\Omega_{i}, i=1,2,…,12i=1,2,...,12 and an external region Ωe​x​t=⋃1≤i≤4Ωe​x​t,i\Omega_{ext}=\displaystyle\bigcup_{1\leq i\leq 4}\Omega_{ext,i}. Such regions are in the heart of the classification of solutions of problem (19)-(21). Notice also from the symmetry of the function gωg_{\omega} that the points BB and FF satisfy the cartezian equation u=vu=v and the points DD and HH satisfy u=−vu=-v. Furthermore the polygon B​D​F​HBDFH is a square.

This symmetry also shows easily that whenever (u,v)(u,v) is a pair of solutions of the system (19), the pairs (−u,v)(-u,v), (u,−v)(u,-v) and (−u,−v)(-u,-v) are also solutions. Consequently, in the rest of the paper we will focus only on the case where u⁡(0)=a≥0u(0)=a\geq 0 and v⁡(0)=b≥0v(0)=b\geq 0. The remaining cases will be deduced by symmetry. As the function f⁡(u,v)f(u,v) is Locally Lipshitz continues, the existence and uniqueness of the solution is guaranteed by means of the famous Cauchy-Lipschitz theory. This will be recalled in the Appendix later.

Theorem 2.1

Whenever the initial data (u⁡(0),v⁡(0))=(a,b)∈Ω1(u(0),v(0))=(a,b)\in\Omega_{1}, the problem (19)-(21) has a unique positive solution lieing in the same region Ω1\Omega_{1}. Furthermore,

i.

uu is nondecreasing,

ii.

vv is nonincreasing,

iii.

(u,v)(u,v) tends to BB as xx tends to ∞\infty.

Proof. Writing problem (18) at x=0x=0, yields that

u′′​(0)=−gω​(a,b)​a>0andv′′​(0)=−gω​(b,a)​b<0.u^{\prime\prime}(0)=-g_{\omega}(a,b)a>0\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad v^{\prime\prime}(0)=-g_{\omega}(b,a)b<0.

Hence, there exists δ>0\delta>0 small enought such that

u′′​(x)>0andv′′​(x)<0,∀x∈(−δ,δ).u^{\prime\prime}(x)>0\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad v^{\prime\prime}(x)<0,\;\;\forall x\in(-\delta,\delta).

Consequently, u′u^{\prime} is nondecreasing on (−δ,δ)(-\delta,\delta) and v′v^{\prime} is nonincreasing on (−δ,δ)(-\delta,\delta). 3 Conclusion

In [Yaping], a system of coupled NLS and Heat equations has been considered for exponential stability in a torus region. The basic idea consists of transforming the system into one-dimensional coupled one by applying polar coordinates.

Inspired from the present work, in forthcomming works, we intend to consider analogoue study with

  • •

    The Heat operator

    ℒi​(u⁡(x,t))=ℋi​(u⁡(x,t))=ut−σi​Δ​u\mathcal{L}_{i}(u(x,t))=\mathcal{H}_{i}(u(x,t))=u_{t}-\sigma_{i}\Delta u

    leading to a nonlinear Heat system.

  • •

    The mixed Schrödinger-Heat operator

    ℒ(u(,v))=(ℒ1(u),ℒ2(v))=(𝒮(u),ℋ(v))\mathcal{L}(u(,v))=(\mathcal{L}_{1}(u),\mathcal{L}_{2}(v))=(\mathcal{S}(u),\mathcal{H}(v))

    leading to a nonlinear coupled system of Schrödinger-Heat type.

4 Appendix

4.1 Appendix A

Recall that in the previous sections, we applied for many times the well-known Cauchy Lipschitz theorem on the existence and uniqueness of solutions. In this section and for convenience, we will show that the generator function used is already locally Lipschitz continuous.
